description: Site: lib.rs:1330-1343. run_chain calls run_cert for each chain position, and run_cert recomputes cert_sha256_of(cert) for each call. The test at lib.rs:1901-1927 pins this behavior: three identical certs at indices 0/1/2 → three hashings. For typical chains (no repetition) this is fine. For cross-signed/bridge CA scenarios where the same intermediate appears at two positions in different chains, this is wasteful. For 'fan-out' validation patterns where one leaf is checked against N candidate paths through different intermediates, the leaf is re-hashed for every path. Fix: have run_chain pre-compute one sha256 per unique cert via Vec<[u8;32]> built before the loop, and pass it into run_cert via a new method run_cert_with_hash. Or: cache by &Certificate identity in a per-call HashMap. Filed P3 because the cost is single-digit microseconds per cert (DER re-encode dominates over SHA-256) and the duplicate-cert case is rare. Worth tracking for when pkix-difftest starts running massive corpora.
title: run_chain re-hashes the same DER bytes per cert position — same cert N times = N hashes
